# Isolated iOS app-build toolchain comparison

This experiment uses one public starter export and compares Xcode 27.2 and Xcode 26.6 app builds. Both producer jobs unpack the exact same prepared archive and configure their own fresh Xcode build directory. The source manifest and original export metadata bind the inputs. The build transcript binds the actual SDL compile and player link to the selected toolchain, SDK and deployment target. The two produced apps must have the same ordinary resources and behavior-related bundle metadata. A separate pinned SDL checkout supplies the existing regression's pristine comparison fixture after each app is built.

The original Files runner and XCTest source are unchanged. Four fresh, 35-minute consumer jobs use the same macOS runner label, Xcode 26.6, iOS 26.5 and iPhone 17e. Their dependencies prescribe A1→B1 and B2→A2. A functional failure in the first arm still permits the next prescribed arm on a fresh VM. Missing or invalid producer provenance prevents either arm from sending input. The normal single Start press and fresh Load tap, actual Files review cancellation, exact restoration, staging and cleanup checks remain required.

Compiler, linker, SDK and producer VM image all differ. The two orders run on separate consumer VMs, whose image versions are recorded. A targeted cancellation on a 26.6-built app would show that a 27.2 build is unnecessary for this failure. A cancellation only on a 27.2-built app would support a limited association in this cohort. Four passes would leave the cause unresolved. The workflow never repeats an arm, and only its first attempt can run. The normal Creator, Goal and iOS workflows exclude this exact experimental branch from push triggers.
